children: India's payments authority said on Tuesday a 0.4% fee would be levied on transactions worth more than 2,000 rupees (about $20) made to merchants via the homegrown UPI network starting October 15.

The charges will be distributed among the firms facilitating the transactions and are being introduced to bolster investment into infrastructure resilience, innovation, cybersecurity and customer service, the National Payments Corporation of India said in a release.

This comes after India changed its payments legislation on Monday, allowing firms to charge ⁠transactions of more than 2,000 rupees. All payments using the Unified Payments Interface have ​been free so far.
The move is expected to benefit banks and payments firms in Asia's third-largest economy, which posted 24 billion UPI payments totalling $311 billion in August.

The NPCI also said payments made via UPI to specific merchants such as railways, telecom services, insurance and fuel, among others, will attract a flat fee, called merchant discount rate (MDR), of 5 rupees.
For other merchants, the fee on transactions above 75,000 rupees will be capped at 300 rupees.
"Merchants on-boarded cannot pass on MDR charges to customers while accepting payments through UPI," the NPCI said.
The NPCI had met with lenders and payments firms earlier in the day to discuss levying charges on large transactions in the world's ​largest retail fast-payment system, Reuters had reported.

title: India sets 0.4% fee on large merchant payments made via UPI
